## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Empty project. Need to build a 2D game for phone/tablet: "Resident Evil 4 RPG necromancer ability". Interpretation: A 2D RPG set in RE4-inspired world (survival horror, Spanish village, Los Ganados) with a necromancer ability. Need to make a complete playable game.

I need to decide tech: plain HTML/CSS/JS with canvas, no dependencies, responsive touch controls, mobile-first. Build with vanilla JS. Need to test with playwright and screenshot.

Let me think about the game design:

Title: "RE4: Necromancer's Plaga" or "Resident Evil 4 RPG — Necromancer".

Core gameplay: Top-down 2D twin-stick-ish survival RPG. Player is a necromancer in the RE4 village. Kill infected villagers (Ganados), raise their corpses as undead minions. Collect pesetas, level up, buy/upgrade abilities. Waves. Boss (El Gigante? Chainsaw Ganado). Touch controls: left virtual joystick to move, right buttons for abilities. Keyboard support too.

Let's design a solid, polished game:

- Canvas 2D, full screen, DPR aware, landscape/portrait responsive.
- Fixed timestep loop.
- World: a village courtyard with huts, campfire, fog, dirt paths, props (crates, barrels, graves, torches). Camera follows player with slight smoothing.
- Player: Necromancer with staff, movement 8-dir, animations procedural (sprite drawn with shapes) or use sprites? Pure canvas drawing with nice vector art. Could use generated pixel-art sprites via offscreen canvas... Hand-drawn vector characters can look decent if careful with shadows and glow.

Better: Draw characters with layered shapes (body, head, hat, robe) with simple walk bobbing. Ganados with torches/pitchforks, red eyes. Undead minions green-glowing.

- Abilities:
  1. Soul Bolt (basic attack, auto-aim nearest enemy, or tap fire). Cost stamina? Let's have cooldowns.
  2. Raise Dead (raise corpse or kill enemy to summon skeleton minion, max 3; minions attack).
  3. Bone Nova / Pestilence (AoE around player).
  4. Drain Soul / ultimate "Plaga Necrosis" (channel AoE, lifesteal).
- Resource: "Souls" (mana) regenerates, plus "Plaga Energy"? Keep simple: mana bar.
- Enemies: Ganados (melee), Torch throwers (ranged), Brutes/Chainsaw (heavy), boss El Gigante at wave 5/10.
- Wave-based arena survival with objectives: survive N waves, protect? Keep waves with escalating count. Show wave banner, pesetas, XP levels, upgrade choices at each level (RPG: choose 1 of 3 cards). That's the RPG element. Between waves, upgrade shop? Level-up choices is enough + chest drops.
- Death/revive, game over with score, best score localStorage.
- Audio: WebAudio synth SFX (no assets) — ambient drone, hits, spells. Must init on user gesture. Add mute button.
- Touch: left joystick, right ability buttons with cooldown radial; aim assist. Also auto-aim so tap on ability targets nearest. Optional twin-stick: drag right side to aim? Simpler: abilities auto-target.
- On-screen UI: HP bar, mana, wave, souls/minion count, score. Pause button. Start screen with instructions, character selection? Maybe pick starting relic? Keep start screen with title and "Begin Hunt".

Necromancer ability specifically requested — make Raise Dead central: kills leave corpses; corpses can be raised; minions follow, attack, have HP and expire. Also "Soul Harvest": collecting soul orbs from kills fuels abilities. Nice loop: kill → soul orbs → raise dead.

Let's structure:
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/*.js as ES modules? Simpler single main.js? For maintainability multiple modules: game.js, entities, render, audio, input, ui. But single file ~2500 lines is unwieldy. Use ES modules with no build, served statically. Need start script? Repo has start.sh referencing RUNTIME_DIR scripts, so the platform likely runs default start. Static site likely served. Ensure index.html at root. Use modules via type="module" — works with static server.

Let me check available tools: node, playwright-cli. Need to run a server. Use python http.server or npx serve. I'll use python3 -m http.server 3002 in tmux/background.

Plan modules:
- index.html — shell, HUD overlays, start/pause/gameover screens, touch controls.
- styles.css — mobile-first, safe-area, gothic RE4 style (sepia/red, grunge).
- src/main.js — boot, loop, state.
- src/input.js — keyboard + touch joystick/buttons.
- src/audio.js — WebAudio.
- src/world.js — map generation/rendering.
- src/entities.js — player, enemies, minions, projectiles, particles, orbs, corpses.
- src/ui.js — HUD updates, upgrade cards, screens.
- src/game.js — core logic.

Maybe consolidate to fewer files to reduce risk: main.js (~1200 lines) split into 4: main.js, game.js, entities.js, render.js, input.js, audio.js. ES modules.

Design details:

Coordinate world: 1600x1200 village arena, walls/hedges border. Camera viewport adapts. Mobile portrait: camera zoom so playable. Use virtual canvas size based on CSS pixels, camera scale = clamp(min(w/900, h/700), 0.55, 1.1)? For phone portrait (390x844), need see enough: scale ~0.55 => view 709x1535 world units. Hmm. Use dynamic camera: desired view height ~700 world units; scale = min(w/620, h/900)?? Let's set base zoom: portrait scale = w/520 (so ~520 world width visible), landscape = h/620. Actually want consistent gameplay: visible width ~700 and height ~700. For 390x844 portrait, scale = min(390/620, 844/900) = 0.63 → view 620x1340 (too tall, fine). For landscape 844x390, scale = min(844/900,390/620)=0.63 → 1340x620 visible. Hmm characters 40px tall become 25px on screen. Acceptable.

Better design world scale: characters ~48px tall, view ~700x700 means 14 chars wide. Good.

Arena 1500x1500, camera clamped.

Player stats: HP 100, mana 100 regen 6/s, speed 190 px/s. Move joystick normalized. Basic attack auto-fires at nearest enemy within 380 at 0.55s interval? Auto-attack reduces control need on mobile. Yes auto-attack soul bolt. Abilities buttons:
1. Raise Dead (cost 30 mana, cooldown 1s): raises nearest corpse within 260 → skeleton minion (max 3, 25s lifetime). If no corpse, nothing (button flashes "NO CORPSES"). Souls (orbs) also maybe.
2. Bone Nova (cost 35, cd 6s): AoE 140 radius, damage 40, knockback, bone shards.
3. Soul Drain (cost 50, cd 12s): channel 1.2s AoE lifesteal + slow? Simpler instant burst damage in 220 radius and heal per enemy hit.
4. Ultimate? Keep 3 abilities + basic. Maybe 4th "Plaga Swarm" at level? Too much for mobile buttons. 3 ability buttons + dash? Add dash/dodge (stamina)? A dash adds depth: button with cooldown 3s, brief invulnerability. That's 4 buttons; layout: big attack? Since auto-attack, buttons: Raise (skull), Nova (burst), Drain (droplet), Dash (boot). 4 round buttons in right cluster.

Hmm auto-attack: could make tap/hold on right side aim+shoot, but mobile twin-stick plus buttons is crowded. Auto-aim attacks is common in mobile survival games. Player skill = positioning, corpse management, cooldowns.

Enemies:
- Ganado: HP 40+wave*8, speed 70-90, melee damage 8, attack windup 0.45s. Variants: torch thrower (ranged fireball, keeps distance), brute (HP 160, slow, damage 18, knockback), chainsaw (fast, telegraph, damage 25) from wave 4.
- Spawn from edges with red mist; waves with increasing count; boss "El Gigante" every 5 waves? A big one with slam AoE, HP 900. Let's do wave 6 and 12 boss? Simpler: wave 5 boss "El Gigante", then continue endless with scaling. Victory screen after wave 5? "Survive 5 waves" is a complete arc but endless after is nice. Add boss at wave 5 "El Gigante", and after defeating, "Chapter complete" + continue endless? Provide victory overlay with stats and option "Continue Endless". That makes a complete game.

Corpses: enemies leave corpse sprites for 15s; max 12. Raise consumes nearest corpse → skeleton ally. Also each kill drops 1-2 soul orbs (pesetas? use "souls" as currency for score and mana pickup). Soul orbs home to player and restore 6 mana + score. Health drops occasionally (green herb) and ammo? Keep herb.

XP/leveling: kills give XP. Level up → pause and show 3 upgrade cards (RPG). Upgrades: +max HP/heal, +mana regen, +damage, +attack speed, +move speed, +minion count/damage, nova radius, drain heal, etc. Choose with tap. Card UI overlay. Multiple pending levels.

Between waves 8s breather with banner and heal a bit? Waves spawn continuously; intermission 5s.

Combat feedback: hit flashes, damage numbers, screen shake, blood particles (dark red), soul particles, glow. Lighting: use radial gradients for torches, ambient dusk overlay via composite? Canvas: draw world then a darkness layer with lighter radial holes? Could be costly on mobile; use limited torch glows drawn additively. Simpler: dark vignette + warm torch glows. Keep performance 60fps.

Art: hand-drawn canvas vector:
- Ground: procedural dirt texture via seeded noise patches, stone path, grass tufts, puddles.
- Huts: drawn with planks and thatched roofs, isometric-ish top-down 3/4. Collision for huts? Obstacles complicate pathing. Enemies need pathfinding around obstacles. Could keep obstacles as decoration at edges and graves/crates that are non-blocking or simple circle collision with sliding. Let's include a few blocking props (crates, wells) with circle collision and enemies simply slide/steer around? Risk of stuck. Use only edge decoration, no blocking props inside arena except maybe a central well that enemies avoid with simple avoidance steering. Keep no obstacles for smooth gameplay; decorate border with fences, huts (outside playable area) and props at edges.

Arena: village square with fences around, huts drawn outside boundary, torches inside corners. Playable rect with rounded corners. Player clamped.

Character rendering:
- Necromancer: dark hooded robe (deep purple/black), pale face, glowing green eyes, staff with green orb, tattered cloak animated, walking bob. Draw shadow ellipse. Facing direction affects staff position/head.
- Skeleton minion: bone-white small figure, green glow, sword; bobbing.
- Ganado: ragged brown clothes, hunched, pale/grey skin, red eyes, pitchfork or torch; blood stains. Draw as top-down-ish bodies with head.
- Brute: bigger, sack hood, axe.
- Chainsaw: chainsaw with red glow.
- El Gigante: huge gray-brown ogre with plagas.

Draw entities as circles-ish with body parts oriented by facing angle, plus walk cycle using sin(t*...). Use "billboard" style (like top-down with visible head/body). Since movement any direction, orient with angle: draw body offset behind direction? Simpler: draw humanoid from top-down 3/4 with head above torso fixed orientation, staff to side based on facing x. Works.

Let me implement drawing functions in render.js with entity type params.

UI: HTML overlays for HUD and buttons, canvas behind. Buttons DOM = easy touch. Joystick DOM or canvas? DOM joystick with pointer events, plus dynamic origin on left half. I'll implement custom joystick: touch on left half sets base at touch point, knob follows; also keyboard WASD. Right side ability buttons are DOM elements; they also work with mouse/keyboard (J/K/L/Space?).

Handle multi-touch: joystick pointerId, buttons pointerdown.

Ability buttons show cooldown overlay via conic-gradient or height fill. Use CSS custom property --cd.

HUD top: HP bar, mana bar, level & XP, wave, score, minion pips, pause/mute. Portrait layout must fit. Safe areas.

Screens:
- Title: "RESIDENT EVIL 4" small caps + "NECROMANCER" big, subtitle "RPG · Village of the Damned". Buttons: "BEGIN THE RITUAL", difficulty? maybe not. Show controls hints and best score. Background: animated canvas? Title overlay over live rendered world (attract mode) with fog and torches. Nice.
- Pause overlay: resume, restart, sound toggle.
- Level up: 3 cards.
- Game over: "YOU DIED" with stats, retry.
- Victory (after boss): "CHAPTER COMPLETE" continue endless or restart.

Audio: WebAudio synth:
- ambient wind/drone loop (low osc + noise filtered).
- SFX: soul bolt (sine sweep down), hit (noise burst), raise (rising saw), nova (boom), drain (whoosh), enemy death, level up chime, UI click, boss roar.
- Music? Simple pulsing bass drone with occasional bell. Keep subtle. Provide mute.

Performance: particles capped, no shadows blur heavy. Use ctx.filter? Avoid. Use gradients created per frame? Cache gradients where possible.

Implementation detail: fixed timestep 1/60 with accumulator, dt clamp. Render interpolation not needed.

Let me plan file structure:

index.html
styles.css
src/main.js — boot, screens, wiring UI, level-up overlay, loop glue
src/game.js — Game class: state, spawn, update, collision, waves, abilities
src/entities.js — classes/factories: player, enemies, minions, projectiles, particles, pickups, corpses
src/render.js — Renderer with world + entities drawing, camera, effects
src/world.js — arena layout/props generation, drawing ground/props
src/input.js — Input manager
src/audio.js — AudioEngine
src/ui.js — HUD & overlays helper

That's clean. Let's write carefully.

Detailed game design constants:

World: ARENA = {x:0,y:0,w:1600,h:1200}? Use 1400x1400 square for portrait. Border 80. Player starts center.

Waves:
wave n: budget = 5 + n*3; spawn over time, max alive 18. Composition:
- ganado base
- wave>=2 torch (ranged)
- wave>=3 brute (1 per 4)
- wave>=4 chainsaw
Boss wave 5: El Gigante + few ganados. After boss death, wave clear → victory (if not endless) then endless continues scaling.

Spawning: at edges outside view with red mist; interval 0.8s; wave ends when all spawned and killed. Then intermission 6s and next wave.

Wave announcement banner.

XP: kill ganado 12, torch 16, brute 30, chainsaw 40, boss 300. Level thresholds: 60 + level*45. On level up, queue upgrade choice. Auto-pause while choosing (pause game, show cards). For mobile, tap card.

Upgrades list with icons (emoji or canvas glyphs? use unicode symbols like ✦, ☠, ♥, ⚡). Use emoji carefully; may render color inconsistent. Use text glyphs styled. I'll use simple SVG-ish unicode: ✚, ☠, ✦, ✧, ⚡, ❖, ⛨. Fine.

Player stats:
maxHp 120, hp 120
maxMana 100, mana 100, manaRegen 8
damage 12 (soul bolt)
attackInterval 0.6, range 340, projectile speed 520
speed 200
dashCooldown 4, dash duration 0.18 (speed 3.5x), i-frames 0.3
minions max 2 (upgradable)
nova: damage 45 + 2*level? radius 150, cd 7, cost 30
drain: damage 30, radius 200, heal 6 per enemy, cd 14, cost 45
raise: cost 25, cd 1.5; consumes corpse within 300. Minion HP 60, damage 10, attack interval 0.9, lifetime 25s, follows player at 120 speed, attacks nearest enemy within 60 (chase within 500).

Souls: each kill drops soul orb(s) worth 1 soul (mana +5, score 25). Score = kills*? Let's show "SOULS" count as currency/score. Pesetas? Keep "SOULS" collected count. Minions maybe cost souls? Mana already. Orbs restore mana, so fine.

Health herbs drop 10% chance.

Damage model:
- Player contact damage with i-frames 0.9s; enemies melee windup.
- Enemy AI: chase player if dist < aggro (always), keep separation from other enemies (boids-ish) to avoid stacking. Ranged torch keeps 220 distance, throws fireball every 2.5s with telegraph.
- Minions: seek nearest enemy, attack.
- Projectiles: soul bolts (player) home slightly? No. Hit detection circle.
- Enemy fireballs hit player and minions? Player only + maybe minions.

Boss: El Gigante: big radius 55, HP 1000, slow chase, slam attack: telegraph circle then AoE damage 30; also summons ganados? Keep slam + charge. Health bar at top when boss active.

Death: player hp 0 → slow-mo? Show death overlay after 1s.

Rendering specifics:
- Camera follows player with lerp, clamped to arena. Slight look-ahead toward movement.
- Screen shake on hits/nova.
- Damage numbers floating.
- Corpse rendering: lying body (rotated shape) with dark blood pool; subtle highlight when Raise available in range? Add pulsing green rune over corpse if within raise range and button ready. Good feedback.
- Enemy telegraph: red arc/circle.
- Ground: cached offscreen canvas of arena (1400x1400) drawn once with dirt, grass, path, stones, blood stains. That's efficient. Props (fences, huts, torches, graves) drawn each frame sorted? Static props can be baked into ground except torch flame animation; draw props separately (huts at edges, fences). Bake most, animate flames.
- Darkness: after drawing entities, draw a translucent dark overlay with "holes"? Use offscreen light canvas at low res? Could use radial gradients with 'destination-out' on a dark layer: create a full-screen overlay canvas, fill dark blue alpha 0.35, punch radial holes at player/torches using destination-out gradients. That is per frame but gradients cached by size. Cost moderate. Alternatively, skip global darkness and just vignette. Add subtle vignette via CSS radial-gradient overlay (cheap). Use torch glows drawn in world with 'lighter' radial gradient. That's simpler and looks good. Ambient dusk tint via ground colors.

Weather: drifting fog blobs (translucent ellipses) and floating embers. Rain? RE4 village is overcast. Add fog.

UI design: dark leather/stone, red accents, serif font (system serif stack: Georgia, 'Times New York'). Google fonts not reliable offline; use serif. Add letterspacing, grunge. CSS only.

Now implement. Need to be careful about code correctness. Let's write modules.

Input manager:
- state: move {x,y}, actions pressed flags (queued) for raise/nova/drain/dash; pointer joystick.
- keyboard: WASD/arrows; abilities: E (raise), Q (nova), F (drain), Space/Shift (dash), P pause, M mute, 1/2/3/4.
- touch joystick: listen pointerdown on #touch-layer left half (or joystick zone), set pointer id; pointermove update; pointerup reset. Also buttons handled separately in UI calling game.triggerAbility.
- Expose onAction callback.

Simplify: Input class holds move vector, keys, and methods. Buttons dispatch directly to game via UI event binding.

Main loop in main.js with requestAnimationFrame; game.update(dt); renderer.render(game). Pause states managed by game.state ('title','playing','levelup','paused','dead','victory').

Title screen: show game world idle (attract) with enemies? Just background scene with fog; camera slow pan. On start, reset game. Could render arena with a few distant ganados wandering for atmosphere. Nice but extra. Let's render player standing at center with minions? On title, game exists in demo state with a couple enemies wandering (non-hostile). Simpler: render world + player idle + fog, camera drifting. Start hides title and starts wave 1 after 1.5s intro banner.

Level-up overlay DOM; game paused (state 'levelup'), choose applies upgrade, if queue non-empty show next card set, else resume with 0.6s grace.

Wave banner DOM element with animation.

HUD:
Top-left: portrait skull icon + level; HP bar; mana bar.
Top-center: wave label + enemies remaining.
Top-right: souls score, pause/mute buttons.
Bottom-left: joystick area visual (shown when touch).
Bottom-right: 4 buttons (raise, nova, drain, dash) with cooldown sweep and mana cost indicator; plus minion pips near raise button.
